chapter: Histology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
question_text: Point out the differences in the anatomy of the leaf of peepal and the leaf of maize.

page_header: Histology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants · 4 marks

steps.label: Type of leaf and stomata
steps.margin_note: Write it as pairs: peepal first, maize second, one line each. A two-column table is fine.
lines: Peepal: it is a dorsiventral leaf. The upper
and the lower halves are built differently.
Maize: it is an isobilateral leaf. The two
Peepal: more stomata on the lower epidermis
Maize: stomata are equally distributed on the
steps.why: The peepal leaf is held with one face towards the sky and one face shaded, so its two halves are built differently. The maize leaf stands almost upright and both faces receive the same light, so both are built alike. Every later difference follows from this one.
common_mistakes: Writing only dicot and monocot. The marked words are dorsiventral and isobilateral.
Saying the peepal leaf has stomata only on the lower surface. It has more there, not all there.
steps.memory_tip: Dorsi means back, so the back and the front differ. Iso means equal, so both sides match.

steps.label: Guard cells and bulliform cells
steps.margin_note: Two more pairs, one line each. Do not explain the shapes here.
lines: Peepal: the guard cells are kidney shaped,
Maize: the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped.
Maize: bulliform cells are present in the
steps.why: Guard-cell shape is a fixed difference between dicots and monocots, so naming the plant already fixes the shape. Bulliform cells are large empty cells found in grasses, and maize is a grass while peepal is not.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two shapes. Dicot means bean, monocot means dumb-bell.
Putting the bulliform cells of maize in the lower epidermis. They lie in the upper epidermis.
steps.memory_tip: Bean for the broad-leaved peepal, dumb-bell for the grass maize.

steps.label: Mesophyll
steps.margin_note: Close with the one-line contrast. It reads as the conclusion of the table.
lines: Peepal: the mesophyll is differentiated into
Maize: the mesophyll is not differentiated.
All the cells are of one kind.
steps.why: This is the difference the examiner treats as the deciding one: a leaf is called dorsiventral or isobilateral by whether its mesophyll is split into two kinds of tissue or not.
common_mistakes: Writing that the maize mesophyll has only spongy parenchyma. It has neither kind; the cells are all alike.
Reversing the layers in peepal. Palisade is the upper layer.
steps.memory_tip: Palisade above and spongy below is a two-storey leaf, so it is dorsiventral.

insider_note: The examiner counts differences, not sentences. Five clean paired differences carry all four marks; three long paragraphs do not.
